Edit exactly ONE file:
  1. docs/CONNECT_INTERFACE.md

This is the document the agni-connect team works from, so a stale reachability claim here costs
somebody a morning. It currently says the HTTP listener is LOOPBACK ONLY and that they cannot reach
the endpoint from their own machine. That is now false.

Update: the status header near the top, the section on how to connect (give the real base URL), and
section 8 "What is not true yet". Add the 404-vs-401 testing trap from the FACTS block wherever the
document tells them to curl something -- they are the most likely people to hit it, because they
will be setting Accept-Profile in a client config and testing by hand without it.

Keep everything about tokens, the refusal to hand over the signing secret, and the connect.kinds
liveness advice as it stands.

THE TAILNET DOOR WENT LIVE ON 2026-09-11. These facts come from the real install and from
verification run from a SEPARATE device on the tailnet, not from the box itself. Several documents
in this repo currently say the endpoint is loopback-only; that was true this morning and is now
FALSE. Correct it wherever it appears.

  * URL: https://edaserver.tailcb2a72.ts.net
  * Caddy 2.11.4 terminates TLS on :443 and proxies to the nginx shim on 127.0.0.1:8087.
  * IT IS BOUND ONLY TO THE TAILNET ADDRESSES -- 100.87.250.124 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::2032:fa7d --
    and this is asserted against the kernel's listening sockets after start, not merely configured.
    That matters because the host is also on 192.168.51.1, 10.10.10.2 and 10.177.7.111; without the
    bind directive Caddy listens on 0.0.0.0:443 and publishes the data plane to all of them.
  * Caddy does NOT bind :80 (global `auto_https disable_redirects`). Nothing this door serves is
    acceptable over plain HTTP. Note separately that nginx's STOCK default server does hold
    0.0.0.0:80 on this host; that is unrelated to the vault, whose nginx config is loopback-only on
    8087.
  * The certificate is a real Let's Encrypt cert issued through `tailscale cert` (DNS-01), CN
    edaserver.tailcb2a72.ts.net, expiring 2026-12-10. tailscale-cert.timer renews it daily at
    04:40. The SHORT name https://edaserver can never have a valid certificate: MagicDNS resolves
    the name but does not make it one a CA will sign.
  * Routes: /rest/v1/* and /storage/v1/* -> 127.0.0.1:8087 ; /healthz and /api/* -> 127.0.0.1:8099
    (vault-api, NOT installed, so those two currently return 502 -- expected, and the data plane
    does not depend on it). Anything else returns 404.

THE TESTING TRAP, worth stating explicitly wherever a reader is told to curl this:

    curl https://edaserver.tailcb2a72.ts.net/rest/v1/kinds                       -> 404
    curl https://edaserver.tailcb2a72.ts.net/rest/v1/kinds -H 'Accept-Profile: connect'  -> 401

  BOTH are correct. Without the profile header the request lands in the DEFAULT profile, which is
  `public` (the bench schema), where no table named `kinds` exists -- PostgREST answers 404 with
  error=PGRST205, "not found in the schema cache". With the header it reaches the connect schema
  and is refused for lack of a token, 401 with error=42501. A reader who omits the header sees a
  404 and concludes the endpoint is broken or the view is missing. It is neither.

  With a valid connect_read token AND the header, connect.kinds returns 7 rows.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED:
  * connect.health returns all zeros. The 19 migrations built the schema; no vault DATA has been
    migrated from hosted Supabase yet. Use connect.kinds as the liveness probe -- it is seeded, so
    it can actually fail, and a probe that cannot fail is not a probe.
  * The public door (Cloudflare tunnel + Access) is deliberately NOT built. Tailnet only, by
    decision, on 2026-09-11.
  * The tailnet is an OUTER factor, not the gate. Every path behind the door independently
    validates the HS256 service JWT. Tailnet membership grants nothing on its own -- and the
    tailnet has other people's devices on it.

Edit exactly ONE file:
  1. docs/DEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md

Section 6 covers the tailnet door and the certificate. Update it to reflect that this is now done
and how it was actually done: `deploy/caddy-install.sh` (run `--check` first, it changes nothing),
Caddy from the @caddy/caddy COPR, the certificate from `tailscale cert`, and the renewal driven by
tailscale-cert.timer rather than by hand.

Two prerequisites belong there and are easy to miss because neither fails in a way that names
itself:
  * HTTPS Certificates must be ENABLED for the tailnet in the Tailscale admin console. Without it
    `tailscale cert` fails with a message about the DOMAIN, which reads as a DNS problem.
  * The renewal service must exec a binary at a bin_t path. The committed unit pointed into a
    service account's home, and systemd cannot exec a user_home_t binary -- it fails with "Failed
    to locate executable: Permission denied", which reads as a missing file.
